workarounds.symptom: [BUG] crewai deploy list crashes or claims "no Crews" when the API returns an error
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(cli): report deploy list API errors instead of "no Crews". Target files: lib/cli/src/crewai_cli/deploy/main.py, lib/cli/tests/deploy/test_deploy_main.py. `DeployCommand.list_crews` parsed the response body before checking the status code, so a failing Enterprise API either crashed the command with a `JSONDecodeError` (non-JSON error body) or was reported as `You don't have any Crews yet` (JSON error body with a non-200 status). A 401 was also shown as "no Crews" instead of asking the user to log in again. (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/9756)

workarounds.symptom: [BUG] crewai+ commands exit 0 when the Enterprise API returns an error response
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(cli): exit 1 when the Enterprise API returns an error response. Target files: lib/cli/src/crewai_cli/command.py, lib/cli/tests/deploy/test_deploy_main.py. `PlusAPIMixin._validate_response` reported every failed `crewai+` API call with a bare `raise SystemExit`. `SystemExit()` carries `code None`, which Python reports as exit status 0, so a non-JSON body, a 422, or any other non-2xx response printed an error and still exited successfully. The 401 path already exits 1 through `AuthenticationRequiredError`, so these siblin... (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/9754)

workarounds.symptom: [BUG] `crewai tool publish --force` still runs git checks and fails outside a repository
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(cli): let --force bypass git validation in tool publish. Target files: lib/cli/src/crewai_cli/tools/main.py, lib/cli/tests/tools/test_main.py. `crewai tool publish --force` is documented as "Bypasses Git remote validations", but `ToolCommand.publish()` built `git.Repository()` before checking `force`. The constructor verifies git is installed, that the directory is a git repository, and runs `git fetch`, so with `--force` publishing still failed outside a repository or without a reachable remote. (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/9722)

workarounds.symptom: `normalize_input_files` silently drops `IOBase` inputs despite accepting them in its type

Target files: lib/crewai-files/src/crewai_files/resolution/utils.py, lib/crewai/tests/utilities/test_files.py. `normalize_input_files()` declares `FileSourceInput` inputs, which include `IOBase`, but its dispatch had no stream branch. A `BytesIO` or opened binary file fell through to `else: continue` and was silently missing from the returned mapping. (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/9626)

workarounds.symptom: MongoDBVectorSearchTool declares Browserbase env vars instead of its OpenAI/Azure credentials

The tool does not read those variables; it requires `OPENAI_API_KEY` or an Azure OpenAI configuration for embeddings. (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/9622)

workarounds.symptom: [BUG] Auto-resize leaves narrow images above provider dimensions
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(files): preserve narrow dimensions when resizing images. Target files: lib/crewai-files/src/crewai_files/processing/transformers.py, lib/crewai-files/tests/processing/test_processor.py, lib/crewai-files/tests/processing/test_transformers.py. Aspect-ratio resizing can truncate the shorter dimension to zero. A direct resize raises a Pillow error, while `FileProcessor("anthropic").process()` logs that failure and returns the original oversized image. A 1×16000 PNG therefore remains above the built-in 8000-pixel height limit. (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/9605)

Tool actions build their tool instances once per flow object (`_flow_post_init`) and reuse them across kickoffs, but nothing reset `current_usage_count` at the kickoff boundary. A `max_usage_count` budget exhausted in an earlier kickoff therefore made **every later kickoff of the same flow object fail**: `B... (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/8424)

workarounds.symptom: [BUG] Crew.test emits CrewTestFailedEvent with no CrewTestStartedEvent when create_llm fails — unpaired scope-ending event pops the caller's scope
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix: Crew.test emits its start event before setup so a failed setup pairs. Target files: lib/crewai/src/crewai/crew.py, lib/crewai/tests/test_crew.py. `Crew.test` emits `CrewTestStartedEvent` before `create_llm` (`eval_llm` now carries the requested spec, which the field's `str | Any | None` type already allows) instead of after it, so a setup failure's `CrewTestFailedEvent` has its opener on the scope stack. (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/8420)

workarounds.symptom: [BUG] Crew.replay() emits CrewKickoffStartedEvent but no CrewKickoffFailedEvent on failure — leaked kickoff scope corrupts later event lineage
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix: replay emits CrewKickoffFailedEvent when the replayed run fails. Target files: lib/crewai/src/crewai/crew.py, lib/crewai/tests/test_crew.py. `Crew.replay`'s execution tail wraps `_execute_tasks` in try/except, emitting `CrewKickoffFailedEvent(started_event_id=self._kickoff_event_id)` before re-raising — mirroring `kickoff()`'s except-clause. (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/8418)

workarounds.symptom: A guardrail that raises leaves LLMGuardrailStartedEvent without its completed event, so the trace span closes as orphaned
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix: emit LLMGuardrailCompletedEvent when a guardrail raises. Target files: lib/crewai/src/crewai/utilities/guardrail.py, lib/crewai/tests/test_guardrail_events_on_exception.py. `process_guardrail` now emits `LLMGuardrailCompletedEvent(success=False, error="<Type>: <msg>")` and re-raises when the guardrail callable raises a non-`HookAborted` exception, mirroring the existing `HookAborted` branch (which keeps its exact legacy error string). (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/8403)

workarounds.symptom: [BUG] Hierarchical crew fails on its second kickoff: manager_llm crashes, manager_agent delegates to itself
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(crew): let a hierarchical crew run more than once. Target files: lib/crewai/src/crewai/crew.py, lib/crewai/tests/test_crew.py. A hierarchical crew only works on its first run. A second `kickoff()`/`akickoff()`, `copy()` after a run, `kickoff_for_each()` after a run, and every `train(n_iterations > 1)` hit one of two problems: (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/8369)

workarounds.symptom: Fix SQLiteFlowPersistence initialization under concurrent flow starts
workarounds.workaround: Fix: COR-891 Fix SQLite flow initialization contention. Target files: lib/crewai/pyproject.toml, lib/crewai/src/crewai/flow/persistence/sqlite.py, lib/crewai/tests/test_sqlite_connection_lifecycle.py. - - [COR-891: Prevent flow persistence initialization lock failures](https://linear.app/crewai/issue/COR-891/prevent-flow-persistence-initialization-lock-failures-during) - [COR-261: Concurrent flow module import races](https://linear.app/crewai/issue/COR-261/concurrent-flow-module-import-races-sqliteflowpersistenceinit-db) (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/7821)

workarounds.symptom: [BUG] Interrupted RWLock acquisition releases a lock it never acquired
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(utilities): keep rwlock ownership when acquire is interrupted. Target files: lib/crewai/src/crewai/utilities/rw_lock.py, lib/crewai/tests/utilities/events/test_rw_lock.py. `r_locked()` and `w_locked()` called acquire inside the `try` that always releases in `finally`. If `Condition.wait()` is interrupted before acquire finishes, the context manager releases a lock it never held. The reader count can drop below zero, and the writer flag can be cleared while another writer still owns the lock. (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/7944)

workarounds.symptom: [BUG] train -f filename error message is inverted
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(cli): correct train filename error message. Target files: lib/cli/src/crewai_cli/train_crew.py, lib/cli/tests/test_train_crew.py. `train_crew` required `.pkl` but the error said the opposite. Message corrected to `The filename must end with .pkl`. Validation now raises `click.ClickException` before the subprocess runs, so invalid input exits nonzero instead of printing and exiting 0. Tests updated plus a new filename case. (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/7903)
